slot.brief: Multi-statement question on diborane structure/reactions (banana bonds, hydrolysis, reaction with water/ammonia); pick the correct combination of true statements

stem: Consider the following statements about diborane: I. It has four terminal hydrogen atoms and two bridging hydrogen atoms, each bridge forming a three-centre, two-electron bond. II. All six B–H bonds are equivalent. III. Complete hydrolysis of $1$ mol of diborane produces $2$ mol of boric acid and $6$ mol of hydrogen. IV. On heating with ammonia, diborane can form borazine according to $3\text{B}_2\text{H}_6 + 6\text{NH}_3 \longrightarrow 2\text{B}_3\text{N}_3\text{H}_6 + 12\text{H}_2$. Which combination is correct?

verdicts.working: I is correct: diborane has four terminal H atoms and two bridging H atoms in 3-centre, 2-electron bonds. II is false because terminal and bridging B–H bonds are not equivalent. Hydrolysis gives 2 mol B(OH)₃ and 6 mol H₂ per mole of B₂H₆, so III is correct. IV is balanced and represents borazine formation.

working:
I: 4 terminal B–H bonds and 2 bridging 3-centre, 2-electron bonds.
II is false: terminal and bridging B–H bonds are not equivalent.
$\text{B}_2\text{H}_6 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow 2\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3 + 6\text{H}_2$
III and IV are true; hence I, III and IV only.

Independent check: I is correct: diborane has four terminal H atoms and two bridging H atoms in 3-centre, 2-electron bonds. II is false because terminal and bridging B–H bonds are not equivalent. Hydrolysis gives 2 mol B(OH)₃ and 6 mol H₂ per mole of B₂H₆, so III is correct. IV is balanced and represents borazine formation.
solution:
Diborane contains four terminal B–H bonds and two bridging three-centre, two-electron bonds; terminal and bridging bonds are not equivalent, so I is true and II is false.
$$\text{B}_2\text{H}_6+6\text{H}_2\text{O}\longrightarrow2\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3+6\text{H}_2$$
Thus III is true, and the given balanced reaction shows IV is true. Hence I, III and IV only.
